── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.

This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Finish this week with a 15-17 mi long run and a quality session—no need for a 22-mile run.
Answers: You don’t need to hit 22 mi before the race. A 15-17 mi long run with a quality session that week keeps the load safe and lets you be fresh for Oct 18.
Next week:
Mon: rest, fully recover from the 17 mi long run.
Tue: easy, 5 mi, keep heart rate under 150, flat route, loosen legs.
Wed: quality, 5 mi, 4×1 mi at marathon pace, 10 sec/mile target, keep HR under 155.
Thu: easy, 4 mi, heart rate 140, mild hills, stay comfortable.
Fri: rest, focus on stretching and hydration.
Sat: easy, 3 mi, walk downhill finish, allow recovery.
Sun: long, 15 mi, steady pace, keep HR 140-150, fueling on gels.
